newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Lupin Lab signs S. Africa deal.
newsitem.headline: Indian Lupin Lab signs S. Africa deal.

text.p: Indian pharmaceuticals firm Lupin Laboratories Ltd said it signed a joint venture agreement with Quatromed Ltd of South Africa to manufacture pharmaceuticals in South Africa.
The new firm, to be called Lupin South Africa Pty Ltd and located at Bethlehem, will be 60 percent owned by Lupin and 40 percent by Quatromed, a Lupin statement said.
Lupin said it saw excellent business opportunities in South Africa in anti-tuberculosis drugs and anti-infective cephalosporin family of drugs.
"The South African joint venture will give Lupin a head start in these two segments," it said.
"This joint venture would provide a strong springboard to penetrate neighbouring markets in Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Malawi, Angola, Swaziland and Lesotho," it said.
Quatromed will provide manufacturing facilities for dosage forms and focus on local production and marketing, Lupin said.

"Initially, the new company will concentrate on compilation and submission of drug dossiers for the registration of anti-tuberculosis products like ethambutol, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and its various combinations," it said.
Lupin Laboratories is one of India's leading pharmaceutical makers. It recorded a sales turnover of 5.28 billion rupees ($147 million) for the year ended March 31, 1996.
